claims.text: The starting material is cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C at strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
Untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr has poor oxygen resistance and oxidizes rapidly at high temperature.
Pack aluminization introduces aluminum into the alloy surface by diffusion.
Pack aluminization of HfNbTaTiZr will form a graded intermetallic aluminide surface layer.
A treatment at approximately 1000 °C for 6 hours in an aluminum-rich powder pack is sufficient to produce the proposed aluminide layer.
Optimizing pack-aluminization time and temperature can restrict aluminum diffusion to a shallow surface region only a few microns deep.
On subsequent high-temperature oxygen exposure, the aluminide layer will produce an alpha-Al2O3 scale.
The resulting alpha-Al2O3 scale will be continuous and adherent.
The alumina scale will grow slowly and act as an effective barrier to oxygen.
Confining aluminization to the surface will leave the bulk microstructure unchanged.
Pack aluminization will substantially improve oxidation resistance during air exposure at 1000 °C for up to 10 hours.
After aluminization and oxidation exposure, room-temperature tensile ductility will remain within 8–16%.
After aluminization and oxidation exposure, yield strength at 1000 °C and strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1 will remain within 163–530 MPa.
